concepts.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
concepts.gloss: Θ gives a tight bound, Ω a lower bound, and o(f) means the ratio to f tends to zero, as limits of ratios.

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponentials
concepts.gloss: Logarithms to base 2 and e as inverses of exponentials, with the rules for products and powers, and the number of bits of n being about log2 n.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling
concepts.gloss: The floor ⌊x⌋ is the largest integer at most x, the ceiling ⌈x⌉ the smallest integer at least x.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits with the leftmost bit most significant, and fractions as bits after the point.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Integers are compared and combined modulo q, and a residue is a unit when it has a multiplicative inverse modulo q.

concepts.name: Division with remainder and the Euclidean algorithm
concepts.gloss: Every integer a divides as a = bq + r with 0 ≤ r < b, and the Euclidean algorithm computes gcd(a,b) and modular inverses from it.

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and itself, and trial division can find primes of modest size.

concepts.name: Permutations and bijections
aliases: sorting a list into a given order
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of a finite set onto itself, rearranging positions, and a permutation matrix has one 1 in each row and column.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: A matrix represents a linear map, matrices multiply by composition, invertible ones have inverses, and Gaussian elimination reduces them to triangular form.

concepts.name: Inner product, orthogonality and norms
concepts.gloss: The dot product measures orthogonality, a norm such as the maximum of absolute coordinates measures size, and the triangle inequality bounds the norm of a sum by the sum of norms.

concepts.name: Euler's formula and complex exponentials
concepts.gloss: e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ is a point on the unit circle, so multiplying by e^{iθ} rotates a complex number and preserves its modulus.

concepts.name: Sums, geometric series and sigma notation
concepts.gloss: Finite and infinite sums are written with Σ, a geometric series Σ rᵏ equals (1−r^N)/(1−r) or 1/(1−r) for |r|<1, and telescoping sums collapse.

concepts.name: Limits, convergence and error bounds
concepts.gloss: A quantity converges to a limit when it stays within any chosen tolerance eventually, and one bounds errors by inequalities, including for the rapidly decaying exponential e^{-πx²}.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction and recurrences
concepts.gloss: A statement is proved for all k from a base case and a step from k−1 to k, and the same shape bounds recursive running times such as F_k ≤ cF_{k−1} + O(1).

concepts.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
concepts.gloss: Schoolbook multiplication of n-bit numbers takes O(n²) steps, and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer trick lowers it to O(n^{log2 3}).

concepts.name: Positional notation in a general radix
concepts.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base, and adding or multiplying digitwise requires carries to be passed upward.

concepts.name: Cartesian product and mixed-radix addresses
concepts.gloss: Entries of a multi-axis array are indexed by tuples, and storing them in lexicographic or row-major order on one tape fixes an address for each entry.

concepts.name: Bitwise XOR and the field with two elements
concepts.gloss: XOR is addition modulo 2 on bits, so it is its own inverse and linear over the two-element field.

concepts.name: Rings and fields, algebraic structure basics
concepts.gloss: Sets with addition and multiplication obeying the usual laws (the integers, rationals, reals, residues modulo q), with structure-preserving maps between them called homomorphisms or isomorphisms.

concepts.name: Fixed-point and exact arithmetic
concepts.gloss: A number is stored as an integer scaled by a fixed power of two, so additions are exact while multiplications and divisions may require rounding to a given precision.

concepts.name: Finite directed acyclic networks
concepts.gloss: A graph of vertices joined by directed edges without cycles, in which each gate computes a function of its incoming wires.

concepts.name: Stacks and recursion on tapes
concepts.gloss: A last-in first-out structure that records the state of pending calls so a recursive procedure can resume after a call returns.

concepts.name: Linear-time tape scans and sorting cost
concepts.gloss: A machine can read or copy an input of length n in O(n) steps by one sweep of its head, whereas general rearrangement of tape contents costs more.

concepts.name: Newton's method
concepts.gloss: An iteration x ↦ x − f(x)/f′(x) that roughly doubles the number of correct digits at each step.

background.summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: discrete mathematics (induction, modular arithmetic, gcd, permutations, relations, graphs), algorithms (divide and conquer, recurrences, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, recursion), single-variable calculus (limits, convergence of sequences and series, basic integrals, exponentials), and introductory linear algebra (matrices, linear maps, invertibility, Gaussian elimination). They know complex numbers with roots of unity, polynomials, big-O and its relatives, and elementary Turing machines with tapes. They have not studied abstract algebra beyond residue rings, Fourier analysis, the fast Fourier transform or the discrete Fourier transform, numerical error analysis, analytic number theory, or multitape-machine algorithm design.
